transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE); Diego Morales (Redwood SE); Anita Chu (Redwood CSM); Michael Lee (CISO, AuroraHealth); Renee Carter (Head of Trust & Security); Tom Brooks (Platform Eng); Aisha Khan (PM)

Summary (auto): quick walk through of SOC2, data retention, and KMS; customer asks for explicit no-training guarantee and PHI handling.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick round robin — can folks say their role?
00:12 Speaker 2 (Michael): Michael lee, CISO. focusing on compliance and data residency.
00:18 Speaker 1 (Samira): Great, Renee?
00:21 Speaker 3 (Renee): Renee carter, running trust and security. We have some HIPAA concerns; Aurora handles PHI and we need to validate every surface.
00:30 Speaker 4 (Diego): Hi all, Diego from Redwood infra team. I'll try to cover the KMS and private deploy pieces.
00:36 Speaker 1 (Samira): Cool. Agenda — SOC 2, encryption/KMS, RBAC & SSO, audit logs, retention, and then Q&A and next steps.

02:05 Speaker 2 (Michael): First question, do you train models on customer data ever? We saw some vendors have ambiguous language.
02:20 Speaker 4 (Diego): Short answer: no. Redwood does not use customer prompts or content to train or fine-tune hosted models. We have contract language and internal controls for that; we can share the clause. There's an exception for opt-in telemetry used for product improvement but it's opt-in and never links to customer tenant identifiers.
02:44 Speaker 3 (Renee): Can you point to how that's enforced? e.g., logs, access controls?
02:50 Speaker 4 (Diego): Sure. We have RBAC across the control plane, privilege separation, and blind data handling — internal SRE/ops can't pull raw prompts without a documented and approved runbook and dual-owner approval. Also audit logs capture who accessed what.

05:12 Speaker 5 (Tom): On retention, what's the default for prompts and completions? We need to minimize retention for PHI.
05:20 Speaker 4 (Diego): Hosted default is 30 days for prompt/response content; metadata and logs are retained longer for billing and security. For Enterprise Dedicated and Private, retention windows are configurable and can be set to 0 days for content, with logs exported to your SIEM.
05:44 Speaker 3 (Renee): So for a PHI workflow we could set content retention to zero and have audit trail only?
05:51 Speaker 4 (Diego): Correct — content deletes immediately or single-digit hours depending on commit; we can also route logs to your KMS-encrypted S3 or your SIEM in your VPC.

08:00 Speaker 2 (Michael): We require encryption using our KMS and customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption. Do you support CMKs and HSM-backed keys?
08:12 Speaker 4 (Diego): Yes, we support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. For Hosted, we can offer envelope encryption with a CMK you control in your cloud account for dedicated customers; for fully managed hosted we retain control but can arrange dedicated or private for stricter KMS requirements.

10:35 Speaker 5 (Tom): Audit logs — what's captured, retention, and how do we get them?
10:42 Speaker 4 (Diego): We capture API calls, who triggered it, token-level request/response hashes (not full payloads by default for hosted), model variant, latency, and error codes. For Dedicated/Private we can ship full request/response logs to your S3 with KMS encryption. Access logs are immutable and tied to our identity provider for admin actions.

13:20 Speaker 3 (Renee): About PII/PHI detection, do you do automatic filtering or redaction?
13:30 Speaker 4 (Diego): We provide optional PII detection hooks and redaction pipelines. They can run before storage or be used to flag content for manual review. For customers with PHI we recommend the redaction pipeline then immediate deletion/unpersisted processing or Private deployment so data never leaves your VPC.

16:05 Speaker 2 (Michael): On legal — we need BAA language. Do you have standard BAA and proof of controls?
16:14 Speaker 1 (Samira): Yes, we have a BAA template and SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation — we'll send that after this call. We'll also include our penetration test summary and compliance pack.

19:40 Speaker 5 (Tom): For the 'no training' pledge, is that contractual and is there monitoring?
19:48 Speaker 4 (Diego): It's in the contract and enforced via access controls and internal policy. We can provide an independence attestation and show how telemetry that might be used for product improvement is aggregated and anonymized with no tenant identifiers.

22:10 Speaker 3 (Renee): Data residency — Aurora's requirement is that data for EU customers must remain in eu-west-1. Can Redwood pin processing region?
22:18 Speaker 4 (Diego): Yes, we have geo-routing and region pinning. For hosted customers we can pin to a region and provide contractual commitments; for stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated or Private in your cloud account.

25:00 Speaker 5 (Tom): Network access for Private deployment — do you support VPC peering, private link, and firewall restrictions?
25:10 Speaker 4 (Diego): We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and customer-controlled egress rules. The Private deployment package supports air-gapped installs with no outbound internet if required by policy.

28:40 Speaker 2 (Michael): We also need auditability around admin actions — SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC.
28:48 Speaker 4 (Diego): We support SSO SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. Admin actions are logged with admin identity, timestamp, and scope changes; logs can be forwarded to your SIEM.

31:55 Speaker 3 (Renee): Regarding redactions, I want to be clear: if a developer accidentally sends PHI in a prompt, what's the remediation path?
32:10 Speaker 4 (Diego): For Hosted, we can purge the content from storage and provide proof of deletion, and for Dedicated/Private you control the storage so you can run your own purge. We also support mutable retention policies and deletions via the API.

35:00 Speaker 1 (Samira): Quick note on encryption in transit — all traffic is TLS1.2+, we can support client certs for Private connections.

37:40 Speaker 5 (Tom): For the pilot, we'd like to start with a small-volume PHI workflow. Is there a way to run a redacted sample with audit logging to validate?
37:50 Speaker 4 (Diego): Absolutely. We can set up a pilot in a Dedicated pool or Private deploy; outcome: redaction pipeline on ingress, retention set to zero for content, logs exported to your SIEM, and KMS-managed keys. Diego can prepare the plan.

42:10 Speaker 2 (Michael): A couple of nitty gritty items — do you store embeddings? Are they treated as PII?
42:22 Speaker 4 (Diego): Embeddings are stored as part of the index if you enable that feature. For sensitive workflows we recommend ephemeral embeddings or customer-managed vector stores in your VPC. We treat embeddings as data and they can be deleted or never persisted for your tenant.

45:00 Speaker 3 (Renee): What about incident response and breach notification SLAs?
45:08 Speaker 1 (Samira): We have incident response SLA tiers in the enterprise agreement. For critical incidents we have 1-hour notification and a dedicated incident commander; we'll include the incident response playbook in the compliance pack.

49:10 Speaker 5 (Tom): Any limitations on PII/PHI in function calling or tool integrations?
49:20 Speaker 4 (Diego): Tool calls that forward to downstream integrations inherit the same retention and encryption policies; we recommend isolating PHI flows to private connectors and restricting tool permissions via RBAC.

51:30 Speaker 1 (Samira): Recap — we'll send SOC 2, BAA template, KMS architecture note, and schedule the Private demo. Action items captured. Anything else?
51:42 Speaker 2 (Michael): Please include a sample retention policy wording and the clause about no-training on customer data for legal.
51:50 Speaker 1 (Samira): We'll include both. Thanks everyone.
51:55 Speaker 3 (Renee): Thanks all.
52:00 call ended
